hero.subtitle: Software architect and PhD in numerical modelling, I design and harden complex systems — data, AI, backends. From scientific computing (Fortran, MATLAB) to production software (Python, TypeScript): one researcher’s method, applied to real engineering problems.

home.cta_text: Describe your need in a few lines — I’ll get back to you quickly.

about.p1: A PhD in numerical modelling taught me to tackle ill-posed problems: break them down, model them, solve them rigorously, then test the results against reality. That is the method I bring to the systems I design — all the more when the stakes are technical and uncertain.
about.p2: I judge software by its usefulness and its robustness, not its sophistication. A good architecture doesn’t need to be spectacular: it needs to stay reliable, readable and maintainable by a whole team — even years after it goes into production, without depending on whoever designed it.
about.p3: I’ve designed and delivered systems in both France and the United Kingdom, across very different technical and human contexts. It left me with one conviction: no solution is worth anything without a precise understanding of the problem, the constraints and the goal. That is always where I start.

experience.lead: From energy to research, environments where reliability is not optional.

services.meta_desc: Backend architecture, data engineering, applied AI, technical audits and consulting — to design, harden and evolve complex systems.
services.intro: Designing, hardening or unblocking a system — where the technical stakes are high. As a one-off mission, ongoing support, or focused expertise on a single point.
services.svc_1_p: A backend that grows quickly becomes hard to evolve, test and maintain.
services.svc_1_d: The answer lies in a clear, layered architecture — Python (FastAPI) as well as TypeScript/Node — tested, documented, built to last and to be picked up by a whole team.
services.svc_2_p: Data scattered across sources, with no common model, stays impossible to use with confidence.
services.svc_2_d: A clean data model and reliable, versioned, verifiable pipelines give it a footing that products and decisions can genuinely rely on.
services.svc_3_p: Bringing AI into a real product means moving from prototype to something reliable, measured and under control.
services.svc_3_d: That means framing the use cases that matter, measuring what actually works, and shipping to production without destabilising what exists.
services.svc_4_p: An application that is slow, costly or fragile — with no clearly identified cause.
services.svc_4_d: A prioritised diagnosis (architecture, database, contention points) surfaces the root cause and leads to a concrete action plan, ordered by impact.
services.svc_5_p: A legacy system ends up slowing every change.
services.svc_5_d: Rather than a rewrite, a step-by-step modernisation — containerisation, continuous integration, production safeguards — to regain speed without breaking everything.
services.svc_6_p: An ill-posed problem, a structuring architecture choice, a topic with high uncertainty.
services.svc_6_d: A researcher’s method — analyse, model, decide — makes it possible to choose on solid ground rather than intuition.

research.meta_desc: Peer-reviewed scientific publications: mechanics, wave propagation and numerical modelling applied to underground structures.
research.lead: Before I designed software, I did research.
research.intro_1: My doctorate addressed an engineering challenge: understanding and predicting how underground structures — tunnels, cavities — respond when subjected to mechanical and seismic waves. A subject at the heart of how such infrastructure is designed, made reliable and kept safe.
research.intro_2: This work led me to cross several disciplines: continuum mechanics, wave propagation, mathematical modelling and numerical methods. But above all it taught me a method: break a complex problem down, build a reliable model, solve it rigorously, then test the results against reality. An approach I bring to every software engineering project today.
research.impact_lead: It’s that rigour I bring to your most demanding projects — the ones where uncertainty is high and mistakes are expensive.
research.impact_1_d: Break down an ill-posed problem, frame it, then solve it methodically.
research.impact_2_d: Turn a real problem into a workable model without losing the underlying physics.
research.impact_3_d: Think in terms of cost, accuracy and convergence before writing a single line.
research.impact_4_d: Explicit assumptions, reproducible results, verifiable conclusions.
research.impact_5_d: Work with large volumes of data and extract the signal that matters.
research.impact_6_d: Systematically test the model against measurements, and distrust both.
research.impact_7_d: Make a complex idea clear to a non-specialist audience.
research.impact_8_d: Sustain demanding, self-directed work over several years and see it through.
research.cta_title: A complex problem, with high uncertainty?
research.cta_text: That is exactly where this method makes the difference.
